subject: botany
question_text: Who is popularly known as the father of Botany? What was the book written by him?

verification.note: Sourced from the Telangana Junior Fastrack botany guide, Chapter 3 'Science of Plants' (book pp.5-6). The botany book prints NO star ranks and NO year citations, so stars=0 and appearances=[] record absence of signal, not measured frequency. Only ONE botany source is held — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper exists in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the board-paper back-test are both structurally impossible for botany: 'unverified' means never yet checkable against a second source, not checked-and-clean. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Father of Botany
lines: Theophrastus is popularly known as the
steps.why: The first half of the question asks for one name. Theophrastus, the Greek scholar who first studied and described plants in an organised way, is the accepted answer.
common_mistakes: Writing Linnaeus — he is the father of taxonomy, not of Botany.
Misspelling the name past recognition — write Theo-phras-tus slowly once.
steps.memory_tip: Break the name into three parts to spell it: Theo-phras-tus.
steps.margin_note: One line for the name is enough.

steps.label: His book
lines: In this book he described and classified
steps.why: The second half asks for the book. De Historia Plantarum, the first organised description of plants, is the work that earned Theophrastus the title.
common_mistakes: Writing Micrographia — that is Robert Hooke's book, not Theophrastus'.
Naming the author but leaving the book out — the question asks for both.
steps.memory_tip: Historia Plantarum is Latin for 'history of plants' — the father of Botany wrote the plants' first history.
steps.margin_note: The boxed name-and-book line carries this mark.

insider_note: Both halves are asked together; a correct name with a missing or wrong book title drops one of the two marks.
